clue.text: Lecturer working with academic author

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer, as on learner plates
on means working, as a machine that is on
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A university lecturer collaborates with a scholarly writer on a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Jack London, the American author of The Call of the Wild; the capital city is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London was an American novelist, so his surname names a writer.

clue.text: Ability to read unknown editor's mark I left upside-down

indicators.note: in a down entry, upside-down means the whole string reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
a caret is the mark an editor uses to show an insertion

explanation.surface: Reading skill is judged by an editor's mark left unclear and upside-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside-down' reverses Y, CARET, I and L together, which suits a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Literacy is the capacity to read and write.

clue.text: Bulletins for modern players on board ship

parts.note: new means modern

indicators.note: on board puts the players inside the ship letters, as passengers aboard

parts.note: SS is steamship
a cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: News reports for a new theatre troupe performing on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' is a theatre company, not people on a games board; 'on board' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Newscasts are broadcast news programmes, reports of the latest events.

clue.text: Rescue ship travelling north encounters circular pods

parts.note: O is circular in shape

indicators.note: in a down light, travelling north means the word reads upwards

parts.note: Noah's Ark rescued the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A lifeboat heading north meets some round seed cases.
explanation.walkthrough: Noah's ARK is the rescue ship; 'travelling north' reverses it, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a vegetable consisting of long green seed pods, also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: He had a hammer and chisel initially to chip inside the ribs

parts.note: Thor, the Norse thunder god, carried the hammer Mjolnir

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: IC is an integrated circuit, the electronic chip

explanation.surface: A craftsman with hammer and chisel starts chipping away at something inside a ribcage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He had a hammer' is not a carpenter but the god THOR; 'initially' takes the first letters of both 'and' and 'chisel', giving AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoracic is the anatomical adjective for the chest cavity enclosed by the ribcage.

clue.text: Pictures of pigs by hot painter

indicators.note: pictures of pigs puts the pigs word first, the pictures word after it

parts.note: hogs are pigs
art means pictures or paintings
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Paintings of pigs by a fiery artist.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and engraver.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was a celebrated English artist of satirical scenes such as A Rake's Progress.

clue.text: Child can follow scripture lessons with a description of rationality

indicators.note: follow places the child and can words after the scripture lessons and the a

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
a son is a child
able means can, being able to

explanation.surface: A child can sit through religion classes with a sensible attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, the British school subject of scripture lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasonable is the adjective used to describe someone showing sound judgment and good sense.

clue.text: Fail to fit in with Tory whip

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: A rebellious member fails to toe the line alongside the Tory whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip' is not the party official but a lash; Tory is the British Conservative party, abbreviated C.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours or schedules that clash do not go together, failing to harmonise.

clue.text: Fighting Spooner's exploding feline

indicators.note: Spooner's signals a swap of the opening sounds of two words, after Rev William Spooner

parts.note: a bomb is something exploding
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A cat goes off like a bomb in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of BOMB CAT and you hear COM BAT; the B of bomb is silent, so the swap works by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat means armed fighting, conflict between forces.

clue.text: Expert with current maps upside-down takes right direction to start with

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: in a down light, upside-down turns the maps word round

parts.note: an A to Z is a street atlas, so A-Z means maps

indicators.note: to start with takes just the first letter of the word direction

explanation.surface: A specialist with the latest maps held upside-down takes the right road from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is a British street atlas, so 'maps' gives AZ, which 'upside-down' turns into ZA.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard is informally a person who is exceptionally skilled at something.

clue.text: Fixation about growth is getting in the way

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fixation word goes round the growth word

parts.note: having a thing about something is an obsession or fixation
a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone's obsession with a skin growth is becoming an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixation' gives THING, as in having a thing about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Thwarting someone means obstructing or blocking their plans, being an obstacle to them.

clue.text: Advanced city with marine distress

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
LA, Los Angeles, is the crossword's favourite city
RM stands for Royal Marine(s)

explanation.surface: A soldier moving forward through a city alongside a marine finds himself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is a feeling of anxious fear or concern, a synonym of distress.

clue.text: Dress to suppress loud music

indicators.note: suppressing something keeps it out, so the loud letter is removed from the dress word

parts.note: a frock is a dress
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Wearing a particular dress to muffle noisy music.
explanation.walkthrough: F is forte, the musical instruction for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock is a genre of popular music with guitars and a strong beat.

clue.text: Mother uses broken toy shark to make dolls

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: broken shows the letters of the two words that follow are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A mother uses a broken toy shark to make dolls for her children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' looks like a description of the toy but is the anagram signal; the answer is the Russian name for nesting dolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Matryoshka is the Russian term for the set of hollow wooden figures nesting one inside another.

clue.text: Revolutionary left announcement withheld

indicators.note: read as with + held: a word for with is held inside the spoken word for left, just after its opening letter
an announcement is spoken, so the word for left is said aloud

parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, also the heraldic left

explanation.surface: A left-wing militant keeps quiet about an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withheld' does the work as 'with held': AND (with) is held inside SINISTA, the sound of SINISTER (left) when 'announcement' drops its final R, so S becomes SAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sandinista was a member of the Nicaraguan revolutionary movement that overthrew Somoza in 1979.

clue.text: Yellow mixture regularly scrubs sailor at Land's End

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: Land's End points to the final letter of the word land

explanation.surface: A sailor at Land's End, the tip of Cornwall, scrubs off a yellow mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes CUS from scrubs; 'Land's End' (the Cornish headland) gives its final letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet yellow sauce made by mixing milk, eggs and sugar.

clue.text: Ambassador key to Hungary's well being

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the formal title of an ambassador
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: An ambassador is vital to Hungary's welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title; H is Hungary's international vehicle registration letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Health is a state of physical and mental soundness, so a synonym of wellbeing.

clue.text: Fossil title title written untidily with biro

indicators.note: letters written untidily are jumbled, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fossil's title label scrawled in ballpoint pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue repeats 'title' by mistake; the blog prints it once, and one TITLE plus BIRO makes the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilobite is an extinct marine arthropod commonly found as a fossil.

clue.text: Frightening people drive up to breed sisters every so often

indicators.note: in a down light, up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: go means drive, as in go by car

indicators.note: every so often takes alternate letters, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Scary folk drive up to breed sisters now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every so often' takes the second, fourth and so on of 'breed sisters', giving RESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogresses are female ogres, terrifying man-eating giants in folk tales.

clue.text: Some cause disappointment backing throwaway comments

indicators.note: backing means the selected run of letters reads backwards
some means only part of the following words is used, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Some offhand remarks can cause disappointment when they go back on things.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters SEDISA run across 'cause disappointment'; 'backing' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks made in passing, incidental comments not central to the conversation.

clue.text: Commander finally in charge after group's release

indicators.note: after places the group word before the charge with its insert

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: in puts the final letter inside the charge word

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of commander

explanation.surface: The commander, at last in control, follows the group's release order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R from Commander, which 'in' puts inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free is to release from captivity.

clue.text: Ringing the coastguard to protect everyone I name

indicators.note: protecting something surrounds it, so the coastguard letters go round the rest

parts.note: CG is the abbreviation for coastguard
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Phoning the coastguard to keep everyone safe, giving one's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' makes the coastguard abbreviation the container, wrapped round the other three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone means telephoning them, ringing them up.

clue.text: I leave idiot for a Greek islander

indicators.note: I leave idiot for a means the letter I departs and an A takes its place

parts.note: a cretin is an offensive word for an idiot

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a fool to go off with a Greek island native.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is the swap: I leaves CRETIN and A comes in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cretan is a native of Crete, the largest Greek island.

clue.text: Sending up a cry of disgust could be sufficient

indicators.note: in a down light, sending up means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a means one
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Mocking with a yell of revulsion might be adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sending up' looks like mockery but reverses ONE (a) to ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough means as much as is required, adequate.

clue.text: Sometimes a challenge to 9 for turning up ill-equipped?

definitions.text: a challenge to 9 for turning up ill-equipped?
definitions.meaning: read as '...?', what one might say to a wizard, the answer at 9 down, who arrives without his wand

explanation.surface: Someone occasionally queries a wizard who shows up without his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is the answer WIZARD; split the phrase differently and it reads NO WAND THEN?, a reproach to a wizard who arrives unprepared.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally, at irregular intervals, a common idiom for sometimes.

clue.text: Cries the country heard

indicators.note: heard means the country name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Wales is a country of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: The nation listens to the cries.
explanation.definitionFit: Wails are long high-pitched cries of pain or grief.

clue.text: Film of major operation

indicators.note: of signals that the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A movie about a big military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Rope is a 1948 Alfred Hitchcock film.
explanation.definitionFit: Rope is the title of a Hitchcock thriller, one example of a movie.

clue.text: Force setter has shortly to concede

parts.note: G is the symbol for the force of gravity, as in g-force
the setter says I have, which shortened is I've

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter is forced to surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter refers to himself as I, so 'setter has' is I HAVE, contracted to I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give, as in give ground, is to yield or admit defeat.

clue.text: Figure on the right in America is a fool

indicators.note: in puts the fool word inside the America abbreviation

parts.note: US is the United States
a nit, short for nitwit, is a fool

explanation.surface: The person on the right-hand side in an American political picture is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure on the right' is the rightmost digit of a whole number, which counts the units.
explanation.definitionFit: In a written number the rightmost digit is in the column counting single ones.

clue.text: Doctor nearly materialised, leaving the Master in multiple universes

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
leaving means the Master letters depart from what remains
nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts

explanation.surface: The Doctor almost materialised, escaping the Master across many universes, a Doctor Who scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts MATERIALISED to MATERIALISE; 'leaving' removes MA, leaving TERIALISE, which 'Doctor' rearranges. Doctor Who and the Master are time travellers from the BBC series.
explanation.definitionFit: Realities in the plural suggests several parallel worlds, as in the multiverse of science fiction.

clue.text: Prisoners to accommodate for a very long time

parts.note: to host guests is to accommodate them
for ages means for a very long time

explanation.surface: Prisoners held in custody for an extremely long period.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostages are captives held to force others to meet demands.

clue.text: Whistler hesitates and passes on

parts.note: a referee, ref for short, blows a whistle
ers are hesitations in speech, so someone who ers hesitates

explanation.surface: A man with a whistle dithers and then lets a decision go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistler' is not the painter but a football referee; 'hesitates' is read as 'ers', the sound of hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Refers means directs or hands on to someone else, as a doctor sends a patient onward.
